• Which domain (`test4.org`).
• Which cursor to start from (`cur456`).
• Which fields to return (`id`, `context`). | | **2️⃣** | Sends a POST request to the API’s comments endpoint, passing your API key in the `Authorization` header. | | **3️⃣** | Parses the JSON response, extracts the list of comments, and prints each comment’s `id` and `context`. If there are more pages, the API will return a `nextCursor` value that you can use to fetch the next batch. | ### Things to tweak | Item | How to change | |------|---------------| | **Endpoint URL** | Replace `https://api.example.com/v1/comments` with the actual URL your service provides. | | **Limit** | Adjust `"limit": 100` to control how many comments you receive per request. | | **Pagination** | If you want to automatically walk through all pages, wrap the request in a loop that keeps sending requests while `next_cursor` is not `None`. | | **Error handling** | Add more robust error handling (retry logic, logging, etc.) as needed. | --- #### Quick note on pagination If you want to keep fetching until you hit the end: ```python cursor = "cur456" while cursor: payload["cursor"] = cursor response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers) # ... same parsing logic ... cursor = data.get("nextCursor") ``` That’s it! With this skeleton you can pull exactly the data you asked for—no extra fields, no extra traffic. Happy coding!
